name: Taiwan Visitor Visa & Visa-Exempt Entry
description: Everything about visiting Taiwan: visa-exempt entry for 64 jurisdictions, visitor visa applications, duration by nationality, required documents, and transition options. Updated for 2026.
tagline: Short-term stays for tourism, business, and exploration
keyRequirement: Valid passport from visa-exempt country (14-90 days) or visitor visa application
targetAudience: Digital nomads scouting Taiwan as a potential base
Short-term business visitors attending meetings or conferences
People visiting family or friends in Taiwan

eligibility.label: 90-day visa-free entry (64 jurisdictions)
eligibility.description: Citizens of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, and most EU/Schengen countries receive 90-day visa-free entry. No application required — just arrive with a valid passport.

eligibility.label: 30-day visa-free entry (select countries)
eligibility.description: Citizens of select countries including Malaysia, Singapore, and others receive 30-day visa-free entry. Check BOCA's official list for your nationality.

eligibility.label: 14-day visa-free entry (extended program)
eligibility.description: Citizens of Thailand, Brunei, and the Philippines receive 14-day visa-free entry under an extended trial program (valid through July 31, 2026).
warnings: The 14-day visa-free program for Thailand, Brunei, and Philippines is a trial program — check BOCA for the latest extension status

eligibility.label: Visitor visa for non-exempt nationalities
eligibility.description: Citizens of countries not on the visa-exempt list must apply for a visitor visa at a TECO or ROC representative office before travel.

eligibility.label: Valid passport with 6+ months remaining validity
eligibility.description: Passport must have at least 6 months validity from the date of entry. Japan and US passport holders only need validity for the duration of stay.

eligibility.label: No local employment permitted
eligibility.description: Visitor visa and visa-exempt entry do not grant work authorization. Any form of employment in Taiwan requires a separate work permit.

duration.extension: Not available for visa-exempt entry. Visitor visa holders may apply for extension at NIA in limited circumstances.
duration.notes: Visa-exempt stays CANNOT be extended — you must depart before your permitted period expires or apply for a different visa status

fees.applicationDetail: Free for visa-exempt entry. Visitor visa: NT$1,600 (single entry) or NT$3,200 (multiple entry).
fees.notes: US citizens: NT$7,090 reciprocity surcharge for visitor visa. All visa fees are non-refundable regardless of outcome.

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must have 6+ months validity and blank pages. Japan and US passport holders only need passport valid for duration of stay.
tips: Temporary and emergency passports are NOT accepted for visa-exempt entry
Ensure at least 2 blank pages for entry stamps

documents.name: Return or Onward Ticket
documents.description: Proof of a confirmed return or onward flight departing Taiwan within your permitted stay period.
tips: Immigration officers may ask to see your departure ticket at the airport
One-way tickets without onward travel proof may result in denied entry

documents.name: Accommodation Proof
documents.description: Hotel reservation, Airbnb booking, or invitation letter from a host in Taiwan showing your accommodation arrangements.
tips: Not always checked at immigration, but recommended to have ready
An invitation letter should include the host's name, address, and contact information

documents.name: Financial Proof
documents.description: Evidence of sufficient funds for your stay. Bank statement, credit card statement, or cash equivalent. No official minimum stated, but approximately NT$25,000-50,000 (USD $750-1,500) per trip is a common reference.
tips: Immigration officers rarely ask for financial proof, but it is recommended
Having a credit card with sufficient limit is generally acceptable

documents.name: Visitor Visa Application Form (visa applicants only)
documents.description: Completed online application from visawebapp.boca.gov.tw, printed and signed. Only required for those applying for a visitor visa (not visa-exempt travelers).
tips: Fill out completely online, then print and sign before submission
Double-check all information matches your passport exactly

documents.name: Passport Photos (visa applicants only)
documents.description: 2 photos, 45x35mm, white background, taken within 6 months. Only required for visitor visa applicants.

applicationSteps.title: Check Your Visa-Exempt Status
applicationSteps.description: Verify whether your nationality is on Taiwan's visa-exempt list and for how many days (14, 30, or 90 days). Check the BOCA website for the current list.
tips: The visa-exempt list changes periodically — always check the latest version
Some nationalities have conditional visa-exempt entry (e.g., must hold ePassport)

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Travel Documents
applicationSteps.description: Ensure your passport has 6+ months validity, book your return/onward flight, and arrange accommodation.
tips: Book a refundable return ticket if your plans are flexible
Have accommodation details ready for your immigration landing card

applicationSteps.title: Apply for Visitor Visa (if not visa-exempt)
applicationSteps.description: If your nationality is not visa-exempt, apply at your local TECO or ROC representative office. Submit the application form, passport, photos, and supporting documents.
tips: Apply well in advance of your travel date
Some TECO offices require appointments — check their website first

applicationSteps.title: Arrive in Taiwan
applicationSteps.description: Present your passport at immigration. Fill out the arrival card (available on the plane or at the airport). Visa-exempt travelers receive an entry stamp with the permitted stay duration.
tips: Have your return ticket and accommodation proof accessible
The arrival card asks for your Taiwan address — have your hotel or Airbnb address ready
Immigration processing is typically quick (15-30 minutes)

processingTime.governmentReviewDetail: Instant for visa-exempt entry. 3–5 business days for visitor visa applications.
processingTime.notes: Visitor visa processing times vary by TECO office. Some offices may take longer during peak travel seasons.

restrictions: No employment of any kind is permitted on visitor visa or visa-exempt entry
Remote work for overseas employers occupies a legal gray area — there is no explicit prohibition in the visa-exempt rules, but it is not formally authorized either
Any work for a Taiwan-based employer requires a separate work permit
Violation of work restrictions may result in fines and deportation
No employment of any kind is permitted on visitor visa or visa-exempt entry — working for a Taiwan employer requires a separate work permit
workPermission.notes: Visitor status is strictly for tourism, business meetings, family visits, and short-term stays. For remote work, consider the Digital Nomad Visa (DNV). For Taiwan employment, a Work ARC or Gold Card is required.

agencySteps.agencyFullName: Bureau of Consular Affairs (外交部領事事務局)
agencySteps.description: BOCA and its overseas offices (TECO) process visitor visa applications for non-exempt nationalities.
tips: Overseas applicants: submit at your jurisdictional TECO or ROC representative office
Visa-exempt travelers do not need to interact with BOCA

agencySteps.agencyFullName: National Immigration Agency (內政部移民署)
agencySteps.description: NIA processes entry at the airport and manages stay duration. For visitor visa holders seeking extensions, applications are submitted at NIA service centers.
tips: Extensions for visitor visas are granted only in exceptional circumstances (illness, natural disaster, etc.)
Visa-exempt stays cannot be extended — you must depart before your stamp expires

faqs.question: Can I do remote work for my overseas employer while visiting Taiwan on visa-exempt entry?
faqs.answer: This is a legal gray area. Taiwan's visa-exempt entry rules do not explicitly prohibit remote work for overseas employers, but they also do not formally authorize it. Many digital nomads work remotely during short visits, but for stays longer than 90 days or for formal authorization, the Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) is the published pathway.

faqs.question: Can I extend my visa-exempt stay beyond 90 days?
faqs.answer: No. Visa-exempt stays cannot be extended. You must depart Taiwan before your permitted stay expires. To stay longer, consider applying for a Digital Nomad Visa (DNV), Gold Card, or other appropriate visa while still within your visa-exempt period.

faqs.question: Can I switch from visitor status to a Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) while in Taiwan?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can apply for a DNV conversion at a BOCA office while on visa-exempt status. You must apply at least 10 business days before your current stay expires. This is the most common pathway to obtain a DNV.

faqs.question: What happens if I overstay my visa-exempt period?
faqs.answer: Overstaying is a serious violation. Standard overstay fines range from NT$30,000 to NT$150,000 depending on the length and circumstances of the violation. Self-reported overstayers receive lenient treatment: minimum fine NT$2,000, no detention, and exemption from entry ban. All overstays may result in entry bans for up to 10 years. Recent legislation has significantly increased penalties from the previous NT$2,000-10,000 range. Always depart before your permitted stay expires.

faqs.question: Do I need travel insurance for visa-exempt entry?
faqs.answer: Travel insurance is not a published entry requirement for most visa-exempt nationalities, but it is strongly recommended. Taiwan does not provide NHI coverage to short-term visitors, so medical expenses would be entirely out-of-pocket without insurance.

faqs.question: Can I do a visa run (leave and re-enter) to reset my 90-day stay?
faqs.answer: While there is no published rule explicitly prohibiting re-entry, immigration officers have discretion to deny entry if they suspect someone is using visa-exempt entry to live in Taiwan long-term. Repeated visa runs may trigger additional questioning or denial of entry.

faqs.question: What is the reciprocity surcharge for US citizens?
faqs.answer: US citizens pay NT$7,090 (domestic) or USD $185 (overseas) for visitor visas due to a reciprocity surcharge. This is based on the fees the US charges Taiwan nationals for similar visas. Visa-exempt entry remains free for US citizens.

tips: Check the BOCA website for the latest visa-exempt country list before booking flights
Have your return ticket and accommodation details ready for immigration — officers may ask to see them
Fill out the arrival card on the plane to save time at immigration
Consider applying for a Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) if you plan to stay longer than 90 days
Get an EasyCard (悠遊卡) at the airport for convenient public transit, convenience store payments, and more
Taiwan uses 110V electricity (same as US/Japan) — EU/UK travelers need a voltage converter
warnings: This information is based on publicly available requirements from official Taiwan government sources. LocalNomad is not a licensed immigration services agency (移民業務機構). This is not an eligibility assessment or legal advice. 本資訊僅依據台灣政府公開資料整理，LocalNomad並非合法移民業務機構。本內容不構成資格評估或法律建議。
Overstaying may result in fines, detention, deportation, and future entry bans

communityTips.tip: Fill out the arrival card on the plane. You'll need your Taiwan accommodation address, so screenshot your hotel/Airbnb booking before you lose WiFi on landing.
Get an EasyCard (悠遊卡) or iPASS at the airport convenience store. It works on MRT, buses, trains, convenience stores, and many restaurants. You can top it up at any convenience store.
Buy a tourist SIM card at the airport (Chunghwa Telecom, Taiwan Mobile, or FarEasTone counters just past immigration). 30-day unlimited data plans cost approximately NT$500-1,000 (USD $15-30).

If you're scouting Taiwan as a digital nomad base, use your 90-day visa-exempt stay to explore different cities. Taipei has the best infrastructure, but Taichung and Kaohsiung are cheaper. Apply for DNV at BOCA before day 80.

Don't rely on visa runs to live in Taiwan long-term. Immigration officers track entry patterns and may deny re-entry if they suspect you're using visa-exempt entry as a long-term residency workaround.

pathsTo.name: Taiwan Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)
pathsTo.requirements: Passport from a visa-exempt country, remote employment with overseas employer/clients, age-tiered income threshold (USD $20K-40K/year), bank balance ≥ USD $10K average, international health insurance.
pathsTo.notes: The most common transition for digital nomads. Apply at BOCA at least 10 business days before your visa-exempt stay expires. Allows up to 2 years total stay.

pathsTo.name: Taiwan Employment Gold Card
pathsTo.requirements: Meet qualification criteria in one of 12 professional fields (salary ≥ NT$160,000/month, relevant experience, PhD, awards, etc.).
pathsTo.notes: For highly skilled professionals. Provides open work permit, NHI access, and 50% tax exemption on salary above NT$3M for the first 5 years. Can apply while on visitor status in Taiwan.

pathsTo.name: Work ARC (Employment-Sponsored)
pathsTo.requirements: Job offer from a Taiwan-registered company. Employer must apply for work permit at the Ministry of Labor.
pathsTo.notes: For those who find employment with a Taiwan company. The employer initiates the work permit process. Requires a bachelor's degree + 2 years experience (or master's + 0 years).
